summary: Backend-only test of strip_imperative_prefix() in engine/query_parser.py, run through the public POST /api/chat/stream with voicetest2026@example.com. 20/20 new tests pass (11 unit, 9 live). All 9 requested scenarios pass: 'help me file an FIR' gives FIR/police steps with no SOS reply and no 112. 'please help me understand domestic violence law' gives a protection-order/Protection Officer answer, not a refusal. 'can you help me with property rights' gives a property-rights answer. 'i need to know about cheque bounce' returns cheque/138 content and 'i want to understand bail conditions' returns bail content. 'My cheque bounced...' and the helmet query still work. 'help me' and 'help' still return the SOS reply (112, 1091). Backend logs confirm qparser candidate_issues are clean for every prefixed query (file_fir, PWDVA, property_rights, NI Act s138, bail_conditions). Regression: test_c1_greeting_stream_live.py plus test_c1_sos_distress_and_adaptive_chips.py = 32/32 pass, after updating 1 outdated test.

minor.issue: Existing perf issue, not caused by this change: for bare distress messages ('help', 'help me'), run_pre_retrieval (chat_router.py:480) runs the query-parser LLM call plus corpus retrieval BEFORE the SOS gate at chat_router.py:1382, and the result is thrown away. This adds about 2.5s and wasted LLM calls to every SOS reply. Logs show '[qparser] ok ... retrieval-bridge q='help me'' just before the SOS template.
'can you help me with property rights' answer is generic ('Please ask your specific question...') and suggests Delhi unauthorised-colony questions. It counts as a legal answer but is thin.

Edge cases: 'please help me, my husband beats me' -> 'me, my husband beats me' (because of the comma, 'me' is left dangling). 'help desk number for women' -> 'desk number for women' (a noun use of 'help' gets stripped). Only normalized_query is affected, but this could reduce retrieval quality. Consider allowing [,\s]+ after help/me and requiring 'help' to be followed by me/us/with/to.

action_items: (Optional perf) Move the is_bare_distress short-circuit before run_pre_retrieval in chat_router.py so SOS replies skip the qparser LLM and retrieval.
(Optional) Tighten _IMPERATIVE_PREFIX_RE for comma-separated 'help me, ...' and for noun uses of 'help' ('help desk').
(Optional) The 'property rights' broad query returns a clarification-style answer; consider improving it for broad-topic queries.
critical_code_review_comments: strip_imperative_prefix keeps the original text unless at least 2 words remain, which protects bare 'help me'. The distress gate uses the raw body.message, so the SOS path is unaffected.
In the LLM success path, normalized_query is overwritten with clean_query only when the LLM echoes the raw or clean text, and original_query is always reset to the raw query. This is correct.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_c1_greeting_stream_live.py (test_help_me_not_intercepted was outdated after C1-SOS; it now asserts the distress_sos template)

Legal answers arrive in the SSE 'final' event; SOS and C1 replies arrive in 'delta'. The base URL is read from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env.
